etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English aslepe, equivalent to a- (“in, on”) +‎ sleep.

definitions.definition: In a state of sleep; also, broadly, resting.

quote.citation: 1997, George Carlin, Brain Droppings‎[1], New York: Hyperion Books, →ISBN, →LCCN, →OCLC, →OL, page 83:
quote.text: The reason they call it the American Dream is because you have to be asleep to believe it.

definitions.definition: (of a body part) Having a numb or prickling sensation accompanied by a degree of unresponsiveness.

quote.citation: 2003, Norma L. Bronoski, Nuns Don't Dance:
quote.text: Louisa sat in the car crying, until her foot fell asleep. She shook her foot violently, afraid the numbness would turn to frostbite.
